1. Data Loading & Pre-processing¶

  • Initializes separate image generators for the training, validation, and test datasets.
  • Normalizes all image pixel values by applying rescaling (1/255) to improve model training.
  • Applies data augmentation techniques, including 20° rotation and 20% zoom, to the training dataset to increase data diversity and reduce overfitting.
  • Loads images from their respective directories using flow_from_directory().
  • Resizes all images to 224 × 224 pixels, making them compatible with convolutional neural network (CNN) models.
  • Processes images in batches of 32 and uses categorical class mode for multi-class classification.
  • Randomly shuffles the images during loading to improve training performance.
  • Successfully loads 18,400 training images, 2,800 validation images, and 2,800 test images, resulting in a total of 24,000 retinal OCT images.
  • Organizes the dataset into 8 distinct retinal disease classes, ensuring balanced preparation for model training, validation, and performance evaluation.
In [2]:
datagen = ImageDataGenerator(
    rescale=1./255,
    rotation_range=20,
    zoom_range=0.2,
    validation_split=0.3
)

test_datagen = ImageDataGenerator(
    rescale=1./255,
)

train_gen = datagen.flow_from_directory(
    "RetinalOCT_Dataset/RetinalOCT_Dataset/train",
    target_size = (224, 224),
    batch_size = 32,
    class_mode = "categorical",
    shuffle = True
)

val_gen = datagen.flow_from_directory(
    "RetinalOCT_Dataset/RetinalOCT_Dataset/val",
    target_size = (224, 224),
    batch_size = 32,
    class_mode = "categorical",
    shuffle = True
)

test_gen = test_datagen.flow_from_directory(
    "RetinalOCT_Dataset/RetinalOCT_Dataset/test",
    target_size = (224, 224),
    batch_size = 32,
    class_mode = "categorical",
    shuffle = True
)

2. Exploratory Data Analysis(EDA)¶

  • Each of the 8 retinal disease classes contains exactly 2,300 images, resulting in a total of 18,400 training images.
  • The uniform class distribution indicates a perfectly balanced dataset, reducing the risk of model bias toward any particular disease class.
  • A balanced dataset helps the model learn each class equally, leading to more reliable and unbiased classification performance.

3. Deep Learning Models¶

3.1. CNN 1¶

3.1.1 Define CNN Model 1¶

  • Defines CNN Model 1 using a sequential architecture for multi-class retinal OCT image classification.
  • Accepts input images of size 224 × 224 × 3 (RGB).
  • Extracts image features through three convolutional layers with 32, 64, and 128 filters, each followed by ReLU activation.
  • Applies max-pooling layers after each convolutional layer to reduce feature map dimensions and computational complexity.
  • Flattens the extracted feature maps into a one-dimensional vector before passing them to the fully connected layers.
  • Includes a Dense layer with 128 neurons and ReLU activation to learn high-level image representations.
  • Uses a Dropout layer (0.5) to reduce overfitting by randomly deactivating neurons during training.
  • Employs a Softmax output layer with 8 neurons (equal to the number of retinal disease classes) for multi-class classification.
  • Displays the complete model architecture, including the output shape and the number of trainable parameters, using the summary() function.
In [8]:
# Define the CNN model 1
cnn_model_1 = Sequential([
    Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation="relu", input_shape=(224, 224, 3)),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(64, (3,3), activation = "relu"),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(128, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Flatten(),

    Dense(128, activation = "relu"),
    Dropout(0.5),

    Dense(num_classes, activation = "softmax"),
])

# Summary of CNN model 1
cnn_model_1.summary()

  • Defines an Early Stopping callback to monitor the model's performance during training.
  • Monitors the validation loss (val_loss) after each training epoch to evaluate whether the model is improving.
  • Sets patience = 3, allowing the model to continue training for up to three consecutive epochs without improvement before stopping.
  • Enables restore_best_weights = True to automatically recover the model weights from the epoch with the lowest validation loss.
  • Uses verbose = 1 to display informative messages when early stopping is triggered.
  • This technique is chosen to prevent overfitting, reduce unnecessary training time, and ensure the final model retains the best-performing weights based on validation performance.
In [9]:
# Define Early Stopping
early_stopping = EarlyStopping(
    monitor="val_loss",
    patience=3,
    verbose=1,
    restore_best_weights=True
)

3.1.2. Compile & Train CNN Model 1¶

  • Compiles CNN Model 1 by specifying the optimizer, loss function, and evaluation metric required for training.
  • Uses the Adam optimizer to efficiently update model weights with an adaptive learning rate, enabling faster and more stable convergence.
  • Selects categorical cross-entropy as the loss function because the task involves multi-class classification with one-hot encoded labels.
  • Uses accuracy as the evaluation metric to measure the proportion of correctly classified retinal OCT images during training and validation.
In [10]:
# Compile CNN model 1
cnn_model_1.compile(
    optimizer="adam",
    loss="categorical_crossentropy",
    metrics=["accuracy"]
)
  • Trains CNN Model 1 using the training dataset for a maximum of 50 epochs.
  • Evaluates the model on the validation dataset after each epoch to monitor its generalization performance.
  • Uses the Early Stopping callback to prevent overfitting by stopping training when the validation loss does not improve for 3 consecutive epochs and restoring the best model weights.
  • Stores the training results in history_1 for later analysis of the model's accuracy and loss curves.

3.1.3. Evaluate CNN Model 1¶

  • Defines a function to visualize the training and validation performance of the CNN model over multiple epochs.
  • Extracts the recorded accuracy and loss values from the model's training history.
  • Plots separate graphs for training vs. validation accuracy and training vs. validation loss to monitor the learning process.
  • Helps evaluate model performance, identify overfitting or underfitting, and assess how well the model generalizes to unseen data.
In [16]:
# Function to plot accuracy and loss
def plot_accuracy_loss(hist):
  accuracy = hist.history['accuracy']
  val_accuracy = hist.history['val_accuracy']
  loss = hist.history['loss']
  val_loss = hist.history['val_loss']
  epochs = range(len(accuracy))

  plt.plot(epochs, accuracy, 'r', label='Training accuracy')
  plt.plot(epochs, val_accuracy, 'b', label='Validation accuracy')
  plt.title('Training and validation accuracy')
  plt.legend()
  plt.figure()
  plt.plot(epochs, loss, 'r', label='Training loss')
  plt.plot(epochs, val_loss, 'b', label='Validation loss')
  plt.title('Training and validation loss')
  plt.legend()
  plt.show()

plot_accuracy_loss(history_1)

3.2. CNN 2¶

3.2.1 Define CNN Model 2¶

  • Defines CNN Model 2, a deeper convolutional neural network designed for multi-class retinal OCT image classification.
  • Uses four convolutional layers (32, 64, 128, and 256 filters) with ReLU activation to learn increasingly complex image features, with max-pooling layers to reduce spatial dimensions and computational cost.
  • Includes a Flatten layer, a Dense layer with 256 neurons, and a Dropout layer (0.5) to learn high-level features while reducing overfitting.
  • Uses a Softmax output layer with 8 neurons to classify images into the eight retinal disease categories.
  • This architecture was chosen to capture more complex and deeper feature representations than CNN Model 1, allowing a comparison between a shallow and a deeper CNN for classification performance.
In [19]:
# Define the CNN model 2
cnn_model_2 = Sequential([
    Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation="relu", input_shape=(224, 224, 3)),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(64, (3,3), activation = "relu"),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(128, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(256, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Flatten(),

    Dense(256, activation = "relu"),
    Dropout(0.5),

    Dense(num_classes, activation = "softmax"),
])

# Summary of CNN model 2
cnn_model_2.summary()

3.3. CNN 3¶

3.3.1. Define CNN Model 3¶

  • Defines CNN Model 3, an enhanced convolutional neural network for multi-class retinal OCT image classification.
  • Uses four convolutional layers (32, 64, 128, and 256 filters) with ReLU activation and max-pooling layers to extract hierarchical features from retinal images.
  • Incorporates three fully connected (Dense) layers with 256, 128, and 64 neurons, followed by a Dropout layer (0.5) to learn more complex patterns while reducing overfitting.
  • Uses a Softmax output layer with 8 neurons to classify images into the eight retinal disease categories.
  • This architecture was chosen to increase the model's learning capacity by adding multiple Dense layers, enabling it to capture more complex relationships in the extracted features and compare its performance with the previous CNN models.
In [28]:
# Define the CNN model 3
cnn_model_3 = Sequential([
    Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation="relu", input_shape=(224, 224, 3)),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(64, (3,3), activation = "relu"),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(128, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Conv2D(256, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    MaxPooling2D(2,2),

    Flatten(),

    Dense(256, activation = "relu"),
    Dense(128, activation = "relu"),
    Dense(64, activation = "relu"),
    Dropout(0.5),

    Dense(num_classes, activation = "softmax"),
])

# Summary of CNN model 3
cnn_model_3.summary()

3.4. DensetNet¶

In [37]:
from tensorflow.keras.applications.densenet import DenseNet121

3.4.1. Define DensetNet Model¶

  • Defines a DenseNet121-based transfer learning model for multi-class retinal OCT image classification by utilizing pre-trained ImageNet weights.
  • Removes the original classification layer (include_top=False) to enable customization for the retinal disease classification task.
  • Uses Global Average Pooling, Batch Normalization, a Dense layer with 128 neurons and L2 regularization, and Dropout (0.5) to improve feature learning, reduce overfitting, and enhance model generalization.
  • Employs a Softmax output layer with 8 neurons to classify retinal OCT images into the eight disease categories.
  • This architecture was chosen because DenseNet121 promotes efficient feature reuse through dense connections, resulting in improved feature extraction, fewer parameters, and strong performance on medical image classification tasks.
In [38]:
base_model = DenseNet121(
    weights='imagenet',
    include_top=False,
    input_shape=(224,224,3)
)
In [39]:
densenet = Sequential([
    base_model,
    GlobalAveragePooling2D(),

    BatchNormalization(),
    Dense(128, activation='relu', kernel_regularizer='l2'),
    Dropout(0.5),

    Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax')
])

densenet.summary()

Result:¶

  • DenseNet121 achieved the highest test accuracy (96.79%), outperforming all three custom CNN models due to its pre-trained feature extraction capability.
  • Among the custom architectures, CNN Model 3 performed the best with 94.00% accuracy and the lowest test loss (0.187), indicating the benefit of a deeper classification head.
  • CNN Model 2 (93.79%) improved upon CNN Model 1 (92.05%), showing that increasing network depth enhanced feature learning.
  • All four models exhibited stable convergence, with training and validation curves closely aligned, indicating good generalization and minimal overfitting.
  • Although DenseNet121 reported a higher test loss (0.557), it still produced the highest classification accuracy, suggesting that it made more correct predictions overall while assigning lower confidence to some predictions or making a few highly confident incorrect predictions.
  • Overall, transfer learning with DenseNet121 proved to be the most effective approach for retinal OCT image classification, while CNN Model 3 was the strongest performer among the custom-built CNN architectures.
